feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration-9 design (score 697.2, best so far) with one geometry change: the seven sensors move forward from y 0.07 to y 0.075. The controller (kp 4.8, kd 0.9, ki 0.5, base_speed 1.3, last_direction, same weights), the 12 mm footprint and the ±3 cm span are unchanged, so any difference can be attributed to look-ahead. The value is inside the contract limit (y max 0.08).

The evidence: iteration 9 kept oval at 20/20 and s-bend at 20/20 after the move from y 0.06 to 0.07, with s-bend faster than iteration 6 (2.33 s vs 2.42 s) and slalom progress up slightly (0.494 vs 0.474). Iterations 7 and 8 showed that the controller gain (kp 5.0) and the 16 mm, ±4 cm footprint each lost s-bend finishes, so the controller and sensing layout are near their limits. Slalom has stayed at 0/20 in every design, with about 1.3 line-loss events per run. The forward-shift trend is the only lever tested that improved results without a completion loss, so a further small step is a reasonable test. The main risk is that extra look-ahead adds phase lead at low speed, which could raise s-bend max_error.

How to read the next race: if s-bend finishes stay at 18/20 or better, s-bend max_error stays at or below about 0.02, and slalom progress rises above 0.494 with fewer line-loss events, keep y 0.075 and consider y 0.08 (the allowed maximum) as the final sensor step. If s-bend finishes fall below 18/20 or s-bend max_error exceeds about 0.02, the forward shift has passed its useful point, so return y to 0.07 with all other values unchanged. If slalom progress stays flat near 0.49 with line-loss events still above 1 per run, sensor position is not the limit, and the next test should change only the outer sensor weights.

Decision: approve. The candidate is the best known design with one small, isolated, valid change. A revision would cost two action runs for a marginal expected gain, and the race gives per-track telemetry for the final iteration.
requested_changes: If s-bend finishes stay at 18/20 or better, s-bend max_error stays at or below about 0.02, and slalom progress rises above 0.494 with fewer line-loss events, keep geometry.sensor_positions at y 0.075 and try y 0.08 as the last single step, since the forward shift helped without a completion loss in iteration 9.

If s-bend finishes drop below 18/20 or s-bend max_error exceeds about 0.02, return geometry.sensor_positions to y 0.07 with all other values unchanged, because the extra look-ahead is adding phase lead at low speed.

If slalom progress stays near 0.49 with line_loss_events still above 1 per run at y 0.075, leave gains and geometry alone and test controller.sensor_weights with smaller outer magnitudes (for example [-1.5, -1.0, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5]), since the signal may saturate at the outer sensors on tight alternating bends.
